2 OFFICIAL GAZETTE April 16, 2026
GOVERNMENT NOTICE
DIRECTIVE FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION
OF THE INSTANT PAYMENT SYSTEM
UNDER THE NATIONAL PAYMENT SYSTEM ACT, 2021-1
This Directive is given in accordance with section 4(2)(h) and section 63(2) of the National
Payment System Act, 2021-1.
1. Mandate by Law: Section 4(1) of the National Payment System Act, 2021-1 provides that
the Bank may modernize, regulate, monitor and oversee the National Payment System in the
public interest.
2. Initial Notification: On January 31, 2025 notice was given to all payment system providers
that the Central Bank of Barbados (“the Bank”) in partnership with the International Bank for
Reconstruction and Development had embarked on the Barbados Payments System
Modernisation Project which would introduce a national Instant Payments System. The aim of the
said partnership is to achieve an integrated payments network, greater system transparency,
standardisation, interoperability and financial inclusion.
3. Consultation Efforts: The Bank has consulted extensively with all of the categories of
payment service providers with a view to ensuring that payment service providers understand the
proposed changes to the National Payment System and that there is a smooth implementation of
the Instant Payments System.
4. Importance of Modernisation: Given the importance of modernising the National
Payment System it is critical that the Barbados Stock Exchange, the Treasury Department of the
Government of Barbados and all payment service providers licensed or authorised under the
National Payment System Act, 2021 to provide a payment service or to operate a payment service,
participate on the Instant Payments System platform on a fully interoperable model to facilitate
instantaneous financial transactions to all end-users of payment services in Barbados.
5. Implementation: The Bank continued its efforts to consult with all of the categories of
payment service providers and recognising that the effective implementation of the Instant
Payments System is dependent on even readiness across the participant network, the Bank has
revised the date for implementation from March 31, 2026 to June 12, 2026.
6. Final Directive: All banks licensed under Part II of the Financial Institutions Act Cap. 324A
and the following credit unions: the Barbados Public Workers’ Co-operative Credit Union Limited,
the City of Bridgetown Co-operative Credit Union Limited and AffinityPlus Credit Union Limited
are directed to take all necessary steps to ready their operations to integrate with and provide
payment services through the Instant Payments System on or before June 12, 2026.
7. Revocation: The Directive issued on the 25th day of June, 2025 is hereby revoked.
Given by the Central Bank of Barbados this 2nd day of April, 2026.
Dr. KEVIN GREENIDGE
Governor
